title: Introduction
Introduction
text:
The Standard-Model paper of this series derives one generation: the gauge algebra, the global group and the quark doublet with its hypercharge unconditionally, and the lepton doublet with the uniqueness of the hypercharge spectrum under a declared premise, Hypothesis (S) \cite{ButlerT12}. The affirmative results first. title: Imported: the dictionary and the exact join

title: Imported: the squeezed vacuum of a bosonic pairing
text:
Let $a_{p}$, $p = 1, \dots, n$, be bosonic modes and $\xi$ a complex symmetric $n \times n$ matrix, with Takagi factorisation $\xi = U\Sigma U^{\mathsf{T}}$ for a unitary $U$ and $\Sigma = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_{1}, \dots, \sigma_{n})$, $\sigma_{j} \ge 0$ the singular values of $\xi$. The squeezed vacuum of the pairing $\xi$ is the zero-mean Gaussian state whose only nonvanishing two-point functions are
\[
N_{pq} \;=\; \langle a_{p}^{\dagger}a_{q}\rangle \;=\; \overline{\bigl(U\,\sinh^{2}\!\Sigma\,U^{\dagger}\bigr)}_{pq}, \qquad
M_{pq} \;=\; \langle a_{p}a_{q}\rangle \;=\; -\bigl(U\,\sinh\Sigma\cosh\Sigma\,U^{\mathsf{T}}\bigr)_{pq},
\]

the sign of $M$ a convention; any function $f$ applied in the Takagi basis, $U f(\Sigma) U^{\mathsf{T}}$, equals $g(\xi\xi^{\dagger})\,\xi$ with $g(s) = f(\sqrt{s})/\sqrt{s}$, which is what makes the formulas degenerate-safe. Wick's theorem gives, for zero-mean Gaussian states, $\langle a_{p}^{\dagger}a_{q}^{\dagger}a_{r}a_{s}\rangle = N_{ps}N_{qr} + N_{pr}N_{qs} + \overline{M_{pq}}M_{rs}$ and $\langle a_{r}a_{s}a_{p}^{\dagger}a_{q}^{\dagger}\rangle = D_{rq}D_{sp} + D_{rp}D_{sq} + M_{rs}\overline{M_{pq}}$ with $D_{rp} = \langle a_{r}a_{p}^{\dagger}\rangle = \delta_{rp} + N_{pr}$. \emph{Provenance:} the Takagi factorisation is \cite[Cor.~4.4.4]{HornJohnson}; bosonic Bogoliubov transformations, squeezed vacua and Wick's theorem for quasi-free states are \cite[Ch.~2-3]{Berezin1966} and, in the covariance-matrix form used here, \cite[\S II]{Weedbrook2012}; the series' ordering dictionary is \cite[Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9}. The bosonic Fock space here is not the fermionic one of the Standard-Model paper.

title: Three faces
Three generations as the faces of the maximal composite
text: The maximal composite is three conformal spinors (twistors), a bound imported at observation level, and a massive matter unit is a two-spinor composite (Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}). Given the bound, there are $\binom{3}{2} = 3$ ways to choose which two spinors of the maximal system carry the mass, each choice supplying an identical copy of the fermion content of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s}, its lepton doublet under Hypothesis (S). Conjecture: the three generations are the three two-spinor faces of the maximal three-spinor system. Corollary shape, at observation level: generation mixing is the overlap between distinct embeddings, a CKM-shaped structure with mixing angles set by the geometry of the faces.

title: Three identical families, mixing by shared slots
text: Let the face-$F$ copy of the content be the composite of two conformal spinors (twistors) on the slots $F \subset \{1,2,3\}$, with the construction of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s} applied to it. Then the faces, three of them given the three-spinor bound of Fact \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}, carry identical fermion content whatever their number: the symmetric group $S_{3}$ of slot permutations acts transitively on the faces and carries the face-$F$ copy isomorphically onto the face-$\sigma(F)$ copy, so the three copies of $(2,3)$, and under Hypothesis (S) of $(2,3) \oplus (2,1)$, are isomorphic. Any two faces share exactly one spinor slot. At observation level, and flagged as such: inter-family mixing is therefore mediated by single-slot overlap, the structure of a mixing matrix with no vanishing entries and suppressed double transitions, the CKM shape. What remains conjectural is only the identification of the faces with the physical families; the multiplicity three (given the imported bound), the identity of the copies, and the intersection count are as stated.
proof: A face is a two-element subset $F \subset \{1, 2, 3\}$ of spinor slots, three slots by the three-spinor bound of \claimref{families.imported-face-valued-bracket-quantum-numbers}. A permutation $\sigma \in S_{3}$ of the slots acts unitarily on the three-spinor system by relabelling, and the construction of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s} is defined on a two-spinor composite in terms of its own two slots and their pairs, with no reference to which slots of the ambient system they are; so $\sigma$ carries the face-$F$ construction, term by term, onto the face-$\sigma(F)$ construction, which is the isomorphism, and since $S_{3}$ acts transitively on two-element subsets the three copies are isomorphic. For the overlap: two distinct two-element subsets of a three-element set intersect in exactly one element, an exact count. The observation-level clause: a transition between the content of faces $F$ and $F'$ is mediated by the operators of the shared slot, so every entry of the mixing matrix is populated (each pair of faces shares a slot), while a double transition (both slots changing) requires leaving the shared slot; no mixing matrix is defined in this paper, and the clause is a reading. The set combinatorics ($\binom{3}{2} = 3$, pairwise intersections of size one, transitivity) are verified by the script. Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) enters only in naming the content $(2,3) \oplus (2,1)$ to which the same relabelling isomorphism applies.

title: Point of contact: what kind of answer three is
text: The number of generations is, in the Standard Model, a pure input; here it is the number of ways to choose which two constituents of the maximal composite carry the mass. The answer is structural rather than dynamical, and it comes with its own test: the mixing must be single-slot-overlap-shaped, which is the CKM texture the condensation section confronts with the Cabibbo angle. The identification of faces with physical families is not free either: the section ``Condensation and the ordering'' shows the faces are $S_{3}$-identical while families differ by mass alone, so the identification requires an $S_{3}$-breaking vacuum object, and the framework has exactly one candidate, the face-valued condensate. What that object does and does not determine is this paper's central task.

title: The alignment computed: the thirteenth refutation, democracy, and one heavy family
text:
Four statements, the first a refutation, the rest its redirection, each at the level marked.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The thirteenth refutation, by magnitude; a dimensional estimate.)} The source term of Proposition \claimref{families.source-term-linear-tilt-mass-functional} is $\Lambda$-suppressed, so the condensate it can induce is $\delta b \sim \Lambda\,\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ with $\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ a length; for any vacuum length between the Planck and Hubble scales, $\Lambda\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ lies between $H^{2}/M_{P} \approx 10^{-94}$ eV and $H \approx 10^{-33}$ eV, that is between roughly $10^{-105}$ and $10^{-44}$ of the weak scale $10^{11}$ eV: the tilt cannot reach $10^{2}$ GeV, the natural conjecture that the vacuum $\omega$-area sets the weak scale is refuted, and the weak scale falls back to the weight question, where the hierarchy has remained since the mass paper's fifth refutation.
\item \emph{(The redirection.)} Alignment requires only a nonzero tilt, and directions are ratios, $\Lambda$-independent; so what the vacuum $\omega$-area does determine is its \emph{direction} in the three-dimensional face space of Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite}, which carries the family ordering and the mixing. The magnitude was never the physical content; the direction is, and the direction is computable from symmetry where the magnitude was not.
\item \emph{(The direction, at structural level, under the Gram-square reading.)} The kinematic vacuum cannot break $S_{3}$ before its own source exists: a face-anisotropic vacuum would be uncaused structure, forbidden by the indifference instrument (Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument}). The source therefore lies on the democratic line, spanned by $u = (1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$. If the leading mass form is the Gram square of the source, $Y_{0} \propto u' u'^{\mathsf{T}}$ with $u' = (1,1,1)$, the democratic mass matrix of \cite{HHW1978} (the reading the section ``The Gaussian theorems'' realises at operator level and successor problem (2) asks to derive in general), then $Y_{0}$ has spectrum $(3, 0, 0)$ times the condensate scale: one heavy family and two light ones at leading order, the third generation's dominance as structure rather than fit; and Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite} is refined rather than replaced: the physical families are the \emph{eigenvectors} of the face-space mass form, at leading order the democratic vector (heavy) and its orthogonal plane (light), the faces up to the rotation the vacuum performs.
\item \emph{(The residue, named.)} The second-order breaking $S_{3} \to S_{2} \to 1$, the anisotropic corrections that lift the two light families and convert the CKM shape into CKM numbers: the family programme's next computable target, confronted in the section ``The Koide geometry''-the section ``The Gaussian theorems''. Everything in this proposition past the magnitude refutation is at the structural and observation levels stated.
\end{enumerate}

title: The Koide geometry
The Koide geometry
text:
The second-order breaking is a perturbation of the democratic vacuum, and the question this section makes precise is: which function of the physical masses is the natural \emph{linear} coordinate on face space? For a vector $v$ with non-negative components and $u = (1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$,
\[
Q_{v} \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\sum_{k} v_{k}^{2}}{\bigl(\sum_{k} v_{k}\bigr)^{2}} \;=\; \frac{1}{3\cos^{2}\theta},
\]
with $\theta$ the angle of $v$ to the democratic direction. The method is the series' own: pre-registered refutation conditions, the natural conjecture first, the data deciding. Throughout, the charged-lepton pole masses are $m_{e} = 0.51099895$, $m_{\mu} = 105.6583755$, $m_{\tau} = 1776.93 \pm 0.09$ MeV \cite{PDG2024}. The charged leptons are the content of Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s} that exists under Hypothesis (S) and only under it; everything this section and the next say about them carries (S) as a premise, and the levels of the results say so once more.

title: The linear conjecture, refuted by data
proof: The prediction: an equal singlet-doublet split means $\cos^{2}\theta = \tfrac12$, hence $Q_{v} = \tfrac23$ by $Q_{v} = 1/(3\cos^{2}\theta)$, whichever vector $v$ is the linear coordinate. The refutation: $Q_{m} = \sum m_{k}^{2}/(\sum m_{k})^{2}$ on the stated masses is $0.89357$, so $\cos^{2}\theta_{m} = 0.3730$ and $\theta_{m} = 52.35^{\circ}$; the script brackets $Q_{m}$ in $(0.893, 0.894)$. text: The natural candidate explanation of the angle is an equal split of the vacuum norm between the $S_{3}$ singlet and doublet by indifference, giving $\cos^{2}\theta = \tfrac12$, exactly Koide. The reading of Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument} closes this route: the instrument equates weights along symmetry orbits and forbids uncaused selections; it does not equate norms between inequivalent irreducible components, which no symmetry relates. Applied to face space it says what Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one} already extracted: the uncaused vacuum lies wholly in the singlet. title: Koide as a nullity condition, for one member of the invariant family
text:
Face space decomposes under $S_{3}$ as singlet $\oplus$ doublet, with invariant coordinates $s = v \cdot u$ and $d = v - su$. The $S_{3}$-invariant quadratic forms are exactly the two-parameter family $q_{\alpha,\beta}(v) = \alpha s^{2} - \beta|d|^{2}$. For $\alpha, \beta > 0$ each has signature $(1, 2)$, face space read through it is a three-dimensional Minkowski space with the democratic direction timelike, and the equal split $s^{2} = |d|^{2}$ is precisely the statement that the family vector is \emph{null} for the equal-coefficient member $q(v) = s^{2} - |d|^{2}$:
\[
Q_{\sqrt{m}} = \tfrac23 \;\iff\; \cos^{2}\theta = \tfrac12 \;\iff\; s^{2} = |d|^{2} \;\iff\; q(v) = 0 .
\]
Numerically, $q(v_{\mathrm{lepton}}) = 0.0062$ against $|v|^{2} = 1883$: null to $3 \times 10^{-6}$ relative (a figure of the original). Foot's $45^{\circ}$ reading \cite{Foot1994} is the same geometry in Euclidean language. The member $q$ is a choice: for $\beta < 0$ the same family is Euclidean, and Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form} shows that the form the bracket construction supplies is the Euclidean member, while $S_{3}$-invariance alone singles out no member at all, so the light-cone reading is not forced by the framework; it is recorded here as the reading under which the most precise unexplained relation in flavour physics becomes a nullity statement, in the vocabulary in which the series' founding definition is that being null is the definition of being a point.

The chain of equivalences: $Q_{v} = |v|^{2}/(3s^{2}) = 1/(3\cos^{2}\theta)$ since $(\sum v_{k})^{2} = 3s^{2}$; $|v|^{2} = s^{2} + |d|^{2}$; so $Q_{v} = \tfrac23 \iff 3s^{2} \cdot \tfrac23 = s^{2} + |d|^{2} \iff s^{2} = |d|^{2}$. The script verifies the chain on the lepton data and the numerical claims by exact interval arithmetic.

title: The chart computation: the sign twist, the bracket form, and the Fourier coordinates
proof: (1) An odd permutation of the labels $\{1,2,3\}$ permutes the three brackets and flips each bracket's sign (each $[\omega^{i}\omega^{j}]$ is antisymmetric in $ij$), which is the displayed twist; $\mathbf{3} \otimes \mathrm{sgn}$ decomposes as stated. On real vectors $\sum_{k}v_{k}^{2} = |v|^{2} = s^{2} + |d|^{2}$. The evaluations: $C(f_{\pm}) = \sum_{k}\zeta^{\pm 2k} = 0$ (a full period sums to zero, since $\zeta^{2}$ is again a primitive cube root), $C(f_{+}, f_{-}) = \sum_{k}1 = 3$, and $C(af_{+} + bf_{-}) = a^{2}C(f_{+}) + b^{2}C(f_{-}) + 2ab\,C(f_{+}, f_{-}) = 6ab$, zero iff $a = 0$ or $b = 0$. A real vector on the $f_{+}$ line would satisfy $\Gamma\zeta^{k} \in \R$ for all $k$, forcing $\Gamma = 0$. With $\Gamma = |\Gamma|e^{i\delta}$ the components are \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}. For the one number: $\sum_{k}\sqrt{m_{k}} = 3a$ and $\sum_{k}m_{k} = 3a^{2} + \tfrac32|\Gamma|^{2}$ (the cosines sum to zero and their squares to $\tfrac32$), so $Q_{\sqrt{m}} = \tfrac13 + |\Gamma|^{2}/(6a^{2})$, equal to $\tfrac23$ iff $|\Gamma|^{2} = 2a^{2}$. Every evaluation, including the cube-root sums as exact cyclotomic arithmetic (the script represents $\zeta$ by its minimal polynomial $\zeta^{2} + \zeta + 1 = 0$ over the rationals), the Euclidean identity $C(v) = |v|^{2}$ on the lepton vector, the Fourier bijection on explicit vectors, and the ratio $|\Gamma|^{2}/a^{2}$ bracketed against $2$ on the lepton data, is machine-verified.

title: The Gaussian theorems
The Gaussian theorems
text:
The chain of the section ``The Koide geometry'' reduces the Koide relation to one normalisation, and the way to fix a normalisation is to compute the vacuum. This section does the computation in the simplest class that has a vacuum to compute: the Gaussian one. The model, stated once. The six-mode face algebra has bosonic modes $a_{iA}$, $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ a family slot and $A \in \{1,2\}$ a spinor component; the face operators are the bracket quadratics
\[
\hat\Omega_{k} \;=\; \varepsilon_{AB}\,a_{iA}\,a_{jB} \;=\; \tfrac12\,\varepsilon_{kij}\,\varepsilon_{AB}\,a_{iA}a_{jB}, \qquad (i,j) \text{ the cyclic successors of } k,
\]
the operator form of Proposition \claimref{families.chart-computation-sign-twist-bracket-form}'s minors. The frozen vacuum is the squeezed vacuum (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}) of a pairing in the antisymmetric sector,
\[
\xi \;=\; \tau\,\bigl(G \otimes \varepsilon\bigr), \qquad G = [a]_{\times}, \qquad a = a_{A} + \lambda e^{i\chi}a_{B},
\]
where a family wedge $p \wedge q$ acts on the family space as the cross-product matrix $[p \times q]_{\times}$ and the two channels are the wedges $f_{+} \wedge f_{-}$, the $S_{3}$-safe channel available to the uncaused vacuum, with $a_{A} = f_{+} \times f_{-}$ normalised, and $u' \wedge f_{+}$, $u' = (1,1,1)$, the channel that uses the descent's orientation bit, with $a_{B} = u' \times f_{+}$ normalised; $\tau > 0$ is the strength, $\lambda \ge 0$ the feeding ratio, $\chi$ the channel phase, and $\lambda = 1$ the universal-strength point. The reading is the gauge-invariant symmetric square, forced by the bracket's gauge phase and the mass paper's $m^{2} = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}$: the mass form is
\[
H_{kl} \;=\; \tfrac12\,\bigl\langle \hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l} + \hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\bigr\rangle,
\]
and the physical families are its eigenvectors, per Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(3). Throughout, $r$ is the freezing depth (the common Takagi value of the pairing, Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}), $x = \sinh^{2}r$, and $s = \sinh r$, $c = \cosh r$.

title: Rigidity: the pairing sector is one event
text:
Every pairing the descent can write in the antisymmetric sector, any complex combination of the channels at any strengths, has family factor $G = [a]_{\times}$, the cross-product matrix of some complex $3$-vector $a$, and
\begin{equation}
G G^{\dagger} \;=\; |a|^{2}\,\mathbb{1} \;-\; \bar{a}\,a^{\mathsf{T}}, \qquad \mathrm{spec} = \{\,|a|^{2},\ |a|^{2},\ 0\,\},
\end{equation}
doubly degenerate identically in $a$. Consequently the Takagi spectrum of the full pairing is fourfold degenerate at every $(\lambda, \chi)$, $\{\sigma, \sigma, \sigma, \sigma, 0, 0\}$ with $\sigma = \tau|a|$; the freezing is exactly one Bogoliubov event with one depth $r = \sigma$, which for the two channels is $r = \tau\sqrt{1 + \lambda^{2}}$ ($\lambda$ is a relabelling of $\tau$ plus a rotation of the coherent ray); the equal-gain identity of the two channels holds to all orders; and the coherent face vector is
\[
v_{k} \;=\; \langle \hat\Omega_{k}\rangle \;=\; 2\,\sinh r\cosh r\;n_{k}, \qquad n = a/|a|,
\]
which at the universal point reads $v_{k} = -i\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}}\,\sinh r\cosh r\,\bigl(1 + e^{i\chi}\zeta^{k}\bigr)$ and in general $v_{k} \propto 1 + \lambda e^{i\chi}\zeta^{k}$.
proof: A family wedge $p \wedge q$ acts on the three-dimensional family space as the antisymmetric matrix $[p \times q]_{\times}$, and every antisymmetric $3 \times 3$ matrix is $[a]_{\times}$ for a unique $a$, so complex combinations of the channels' wedges are of the stated form. The identity \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}: $([a]_{\times}w)_{i} = \varepsilon_{ijk}a_{j}w_{k}$ and $[a]_{\times}^{\dagger} = -[\bar a]_{\times}$, so $GG^{\dagger}w = -a \times (\bar a \times w) = |a|^{2}w - \bar{a}\,(a \cdot w)$ by the triple-product identity, which is \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}. Its spectrum: on the two-dimensional space $\{w : a \cdot w = 0\}$, the Hermitian orthogonal complement of $\bar a$, the second term vanishes, eigenvalue $|a|^{2}$ twice; and $GG^{\dagger}\bar{a} = |a|^{2}\bar{a} - \bar{a}\,(a \cdot \bar{a}) = 0$ since $a \cdot \bar{a} = |a|^{2}$, the exact zero. Tensoring with the spinor $\varepsilon$ (unitary, $2 \times 2$) gives $\xi\xi^{\dagger} = \tau^{2}\,GG^{\dagger} \otimes \mathbb{1}$, so the singular values of $\xi$, which are its Takagi values, are $\{\sigma, \sigma, \sigma, \sigma, 0, 0\}$ with $\sigma = \tau|a|$, fourfold degenerate for every channel combination. The two channels: $f_{+} \times f_{-} = (\zeta^{2} - \zeta)(1,1,1)$ and $u' \times f_{+} = (\zeta^{2} - \zeta)f_{+}$ with $\zeta^{2} - \zeta = -i\sqrt{3}$, so the normalised channel vectors are $a_{A} = -i(1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$ and $a_{B} = -if_{+}/\sqrt{3}$, Hermitian-orthogonal ($\sum_{k}\zeta^{k} = 0$), whence $|a|^{2} = 1 + \lambda^{2}$ and $r = \tau\sqrt{1+\lambda^{2}}$. Because the nonzero Takagi values coincide, every function of the pairing applied in the Takagi basis (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}) is a scalar multiple of $\xi$ on its range: $M = -\tfrac{\sinh\sigma\cosh\sigma}{\sigma}\,\xi = -sc\,\hat\xi$ with $\hat\xi = \xi/\sigma$, and $N = s^{2}\,\overline{\Pi}$ with $\Pi = \hat\xi\hat\xi^{\dagger} = R \otimes \mathbb{1}$, $R = \mathbb{1} - \bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}}$ the projector onto $\{w : a \cdot w = 0\}$; this is the all-orders equal-gain statement, since both channels are fed through the same scalar. The coherent vector: $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}\rangle = \sum_{pq}\Theta_{k}[p,q]M_{pq}$ with $\Theta_{k} = \tfrac12(E_{k} \otimes \varepsilon)$, $(E_{k})_{ij} = \varepsilon_{kij}$, so $\langle\hat\Omega_{k}\rangle = -\tfrac{sc}{2|a|}\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}G)\,\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = \tfrac{sc}{|a|}\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}G) = 2sc\,a_{k}/|a|$, using $\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = -2$ and $\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}[a]_{\times}) = \sum_{ij}\varepsilon_{kij}\varepsilon_{jmi}a_{m} = 2a_{k}$. At the universal point $n = (a_{A} + e^{i\chi}a_{B})/\sqrt{2} = -i(1 + e^{i\chi}\zeta^{k})/\sqrt{6}$, which is the displayed formula. The spectrum identity \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}, the channel cross products, the orthogonality, and the coherent-vector formula are verified by the script in exact cyclotomic arithmetic.

title: The skeleton: rank one plus the ordering shift, and the unbreakable $S_{2}$
proof:
Write $\hat\Omega_{k} = \sum_{pq}\Theta_{k}[p,q]\,a_{p}a_{q}$ with $\Theta_{k} = \tfrac12(E_{k} \otimes \varepsilon)$ symmetric and real, and put $\omega_{k} = \langle\hat\Omega_{k}\rangle = \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}M)$. By Wick's theorem (Fact \claimref{families.imported-squeezed-vacuum-bosonic-pairing}), using the symmetry of $\Theta_{l}$ to merge the two $NN$ terms,
\[
\langle\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\hat\Omega_{l}\rangle = 2\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}\bigr) + \bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l}, \qquad
\langle\hat\Omega_{l}\hat\Omega_{k}^{\dagger}\rangle = 2\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Theta_{l}(\mathbb{1}+N^{\mathsf{T}})\Theta_{k}(\mathbb{1}+N)\bigr) + \omega_{l}\bar\omega_{k},
\]
so that
\[
H_{kl} \;=\; \bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l} + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}N) + 2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}),
\]
four pieces. Insert the Gaussian data of Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event}: $N = s^{2}\,\overline{R} \otimes \mathbb{1}$, $N^{\mathsf{T}} = s^{2}\,R \otimes \mathbb{1}$ with $R = \mathbb{1} - \bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}}$, and $\omega_{k} = 2sc\,n_{k}$. Every trace factorises over the tensor product, with $\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = -2$ on the spinor factor, and on the family factor the only identities needed are $E_{k}E_{l} = e_{l}e_{k}^{\mathsf{T}} - \delta_{kl}\mathbb{1}$ (from $\sum_{j}\varepsilon_{kij}\varepsilon_{ljm} = \delta_{km}\delta_{il} - \delta_{kl}\delta_{im}$), hence $\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}) = -2\delta_{kl}$ and $\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}X) = X_{kl} - \delta_{kl}\,\mathrm{tr}X$, and $n^{\mathsf{T}}E_{k}n = 0$ (antisymmetry). The pieces:
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}) &= \tfrac14\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{l}E_{k})\,\mathrm{tr}(\varepsilon\varepsilon) = \delta_{kl},\\
\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) + \mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{l}\Theta_{k}N) &= -\tfrac{s^{2}}{2}\bigl[\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}E_{l}R) + \mathrm{tr}(E_{l}E_{k}\overline{R})\bigr]\\
&= -\tfrac{s^{2}}{2}\bigl[(R_{kl} - 2\delta_{kl}) + (\overline{R}_{lk} - 2\delta_{kl})\bigr] = s^{2}\delta_{kl} + s^{2}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},\\
2\,\mathrm{tr}(\Theta_{k}N\Theta_{l}N^{\mathsf{T}}) &= -s^{4}\,\mathrm{tr}(E_{k}\overline{R}E_{l}R)\\
&= -s^{4}\bigl[-2\delta_{kl} - (n_{l}\bar{n}_{k} - \delta_{kl}) - (\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} - \delta_{kl}) + (n^{\mathsf{T}}E_{k}n)(\bar{n}^{\mathsf{T}}E_{l}\bar{n})\bigr]\\
&= 2s^{4}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},\\
\bar\omega_{k}\omega_{l} &= 4s^{2}c^{2}\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l},
\end{align*}
using $\mathrm{tr}\,R = 2$, $\overline{R}_{lk} = R_{kl}$, and in the third line the expansion of $\overline{R} = \mathbb{1} - n\bar{n}^{\mathsf{T}}$ and $R = \mathbb{1} - \bar{n}n^{\mathsf{T}}$ into four traces. Summing, $H_{kl} = (1 + s^{2})\delta_{kl} + (s^{2} + 2s^{4} + 4s^{2}c^{2})\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l} = c^{2}\delta_{kl} + x(5 + 6x)\,\bar{n}_{k}n_{l}$ with $c^{2} = 1 + x$, which is \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}; the heavy eigenvalue is $1 + x + 5x + 6x^{2}$ and the trace is $3(1+x) + 5x + 6x^{2}$. title: The classification: the displaced-Gaussian class is solved, at the level of its weakest clause
text:
The candidate inventory for the $S_{2} \to 1$ splitting within the displaced-Gaussian class of the six-mode face algebra has three entries, of which the first is closed by theorem and the other two by flagged preliminary computation:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(More pairing channels: closed by theorem.)} By Proposition \claimref{families.rigidity-pairing-sector-one-event} and Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift}, every antisymmetric pairing is one fourfold-degenerate event with an exactly degenerate light pair. No pairing the descent can write splits the degenerate pair.
\item \emph{(The symmetric-spinor noise channel: preliminary computation.)} Preliminary computation by the methods of this section, in a displaced-Gaussian computation checked against exact Fock-space evaluation, indicates that the one pairing outside the $\varepsilon$-sector splits the pair but cannot reach the physical ratio pair $(m_{\mu}/m_{e}, m_{\tau}/m_{\mu}) = (206.77, 16.82)$: the best attainable point found is $(101, 19)$, far from Koide, with the deformation of $Q$ excluding the route along the way. The scan is not reproduced by this paper's script and the clause carries that level.
\item \emph{(The condensate means: preliminary computation.)} The same computation indicates that nonzero means with the flag-forced equal-amplitude form cap the split at $1.2032$, short of $206.77$ by a factor of $172$; and that with free amplitudes the physical spectrum is reachable exactly at every depth, with the solution itself showing why: the required leg asymmetry is $g_{1}/g_{2} \approx 207.5$, the muon-electron ratio relabelled, with sensitivity of the predicted split to the free parameter exactly $1$ and the heavy mass not responding at all. A mechanism whose parameters are the answer derives nothing. Same level as (2).
\end{enumerate}
The terminal statement, at the level of its weakest clause: the displaced-Gaussian class is solved; its entire output is the rank-one-plus-shift skeleton (rigidly one event, $S_{2}$-exact, by theorem), bounded Koide-incompatible perturbations of it, and free mean textures that are the mass data under another name. The physical charged-lepton spectrum lies in the class only as a relabelling of itself. The remaining route is named and constrained: a non-Gaussian frozen vacuum or a larger algebra, required to produce the number $207$ from caused structure, with the relabelling signature (unit sensitivity to a free parameter) as the refutation condition on every future candidate.

title: The terminal state
One open problem in three forms
text: The flavour problem, in this framework and at the displaced-Gaussian state class, is not an undiscovered operator: it is the numbers layer, three times over. The split ($m_{\mu}/m_{e} \approx 207$), the angle ($45^{\circ}$, present only through the depth), and the depth ($x^{*} \approx 769$) are one open problem in three forms, and the Gaussian vacuum treats all three as inputs. The registered open problem is the non-Gaussian completion: structure beyond the class (a non-Gaussian frozen vacuum with higher cumulants, or a larger algebra) that produces the $207$ from caused structure, constrained by the relabelling-signature refutation condition of Proposition \claimref{families.classification-displaced-gaussian-class-solved-level}, and required to preserve the skeleton of Theorem \claimref{families.skeleton-rank-one-plus-ordering-shift} and to introduce no second free number. Until it is solved, the Koide relation stands within the framework as what the chain of refutations has made it: a $10^{-5}$-precision measurement of a frozen vacuum whose structure is theorems and whose numbers remain to be derived.

title: Koide as instrument
text: Whatever the mechanism, the relation's observed exactness is a measurement of the frozen vacuum's face sector. By $Q_{v} = 1/(3\cos^{2}\theta)$, $\delta Q/Q = 2\tan\theta\,\delta\theta$, so at $\theta = 45^{\circ}$ the relative deviation $3.3 \times 10^{-6}$ of Proposition \claimref{families.linear-conjecture-refuted-data} puts the angle of the $\sqrt{m}$ vector to the democratic axis at $45^{\circ}$ minus $1.7 \times 10^{-6}$ radians on the central masses, an exact-arithmetic consequence the script checks. The $\pm 0.09$ MeV on $m_{\tau}$ moves the angle by about $3.8 \times 10^{-6}$ radians, so the offset the instrument reads is below its resolution: the data are consistent with exactly $45^{\circ}$. Any mechanism that moves the singlet and doublet norms together leaves $\theta$ fixed and is invisible to the relation; what it measures is the differential effect on the two components. Whatever else it is, the relation is a precision instrument reading the frozen vacuum's face sector.

title: Selectivity, at observation level
text: The quarks fail the relation at pole masses, and under Hypothesis (S) the framework contains a structural asymmetry between leptons and quarks: the leptons are whole-spinor states (each a whole conformal spinor), colour singlets whose brackets are physical masses undressed, while quarks are pair-level cells, their masses dressed by the strong interaction (Fact \claimref{families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s}). The asymmetry does not account for the quarks' failure at the level of the known strong dressing: a dressing that is flavour-blind or favours the lighter quarks can only lower the Koide quotient, the measured quark quotients already exceed $\tfrac23$ in both sectors at every standard mass definition, and perturbative QCD running, pole conversion and constituent dressing are of that kind (argued, standard QCD), so they cannot turn Koide brackets into the measured quark masses; a Koide bracket would need a dressing favouring the heaviest quark over a lighter one by a factor of at least $1.88$ (down sector) and $8.67$ (up sector, own-scale masses), and a dressing that raises the middle mass and lowers the lightest relative to the heaviest is not excluded (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mass-ordered-dressing-cannot-spoil-koide}). The neutrinos are exempt structurally: their masses are seesaw-composed, quadratic again in the bracket-linear objects, so the null condition constrains the unobservable Dirac layer and imposes nothing on the physical $m_{\nu}$ (the neutrino paper T15 \cite{ButlerT15} carries the neutrino mass sector and does not treat the relation; the exemption is this paper's observation). Both statements are flagged at observation level: the first records the quarks' failure and that the strong dressing, as far as it is known, does not explain it, so whether the quark brackets satisfy the relation at all is open; the second is a consistency, not a derivation.

title: The absolute scale: a clean negative result
text: The other half of the weight problem, why $\mathrm{Im}\,w_{e} \sim 10^{38}$ at all (Fact \claimref{families.imported-dictionary-exact-join}), resists every structural attack attempted: expressing the imaginary weights as powers of $N$ finds no clean exponent for the electron or the weak scale, and the one suggestive scaling (a hadronic weight $\mathrm{Im}\,w_{h} \sim N^{2/3}$ with $N = M_{P}/H$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}, equivalently $m_{h} \sim (M_{P}^{2}H)^{1/3} \approx 5 \times 10^{7}$ eV on the inputs of Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(1), the pion-scale coincidence) reduces to the Zel'dovich-Weinberg coincidence, in the literature since 1967 \cite{Zeldovich1967, Weinberg1972}, and therefore fails the series' prior-art condition. Counting the tower's hyperbolic pairs, mode-count ratios, and fine-structure powers all fail their own refutation conditions. The absolute hierarchy remains as the fifth and thirteenth refutations left it: one unexplained number, restated, with a map of the routes that do not work.

title: Why the kinematic attacks had to fail
text:
On the principal series $w = -\tfrac32 \pm i\nu$ with $\nu = m/H + O(H/m)$ (Fact \claimref{families.imported-dictionary-exact-join}), so that $\mathrm{Im}\,w$ is the mass in Hubble units and, trivially,
\[
\mathrm{Im}\,w \;=\; \frac{m}{H} \;=\; N \cdot \frac{m}{M_{P}} .
\]
Under the rescaling of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}, $\Lambda \to \kappa^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, the two factors have different status: $N \to N/\kappa$, which is the proved clause of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}; and $m/M_{P}$ is invariant, $m$ fixed while $H \to \kappa H$, which is the observation-level reading of \cite[Prop.~7.6(1)]{ButlerT12} recorded in Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number} and is the premise of this proposition, so that the proposition stands at that level. Granting it, $\mathrm{Im}\,w \to \mathrm{Im}\,w/\kappa$, and consequently any relation $\mathrm{Im}\,w = f(N)$ that holds across the family of frozen points must satisfy $f(N/\kappa) = f(N)/\kappa$ for every $\kappa > 0$, which forces $f$ linear, $\mathrm{Im}\,w = cN$ with $c = m/M_{P}$ a rescaling invariant. A power law $\mathrm{Im}\,w \sim N^{a}$ with $a \neq 1$, the hadronic $N^{2/3}$ of Observation \claimref{families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-result} or any other clean exponent, is the relation $m/M_{P} \sim N^{a - 1}$ between two independent continuous moduli of the kinematic layer, which by Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number} fixes neither. So no kinematic attack can give an exponent other than one, and the exponent one says only that $m/M_{P}$ is a number. The Zel'dovich-Weinberg coincidence, $m_{h}^{3} \sim M_{P}^{2}H$, is $m_{h}/M_{P} \sim N^{-1/3}$ and can be, in this framework, only a coincidence of the present epoch or a dynamical relation among couplings, never a kinematic theorem. The map of failed routes in Observation \claimref{families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-result} is thereby closed by a proof rather than left open: the absolute scale dissolves into three separately assigned pieces, $N$ (the cosmological constant, behind the promotion decision and then the descent measure, the Standard-Model paper's successor (5)), the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2 \times 10^{-17}$ (a second rescaling-invariant modulus, the Standard-Model paper's successor (1), so kinematically not a function of $N$), and the Yukawa pattern, $y_{e} \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ and the ratios (the section ``The weight spectrum: the order of operations''). Only the third has computable structure available; and the second-order breaking and the CKM angles, being ratios and angles, are invariant under the rescaling and independent of the first two, so they depend on the third alone.

title: The weight spectrum: the order of operations
The weight spectrum: the order of operations
text:
The Standard-Model paper derives the tree relations $m_{
u} = m_{u}$, $m_{e} = m_{d}$ from a vev in the rung directions of the $10$ and proves three no-go theorems on what can dress them \cite[Cor.~9.25, Thms.~9.31, 9.33, 9.35]{ButlerT12}. This section locates in the module the one direction that carries the second family's factor on a single family, records the grade-three direction that can carry it between families, and fixes the order of operations of the matter programme: the two-term structure first, the family breaking second, the order the capstone's table of open directions records \cite[Table~4]{ButlerT17}. Throughout, the module is the Standard-Model paper's two-rung module \cite[Def.~9.8]{ButlerT12}, realised on $\Lambda^{ ullet}\C^{5}$ with $v_{a}$ acting by wedge and $w_{a}$ by contraction, modes $1, 2, 3$ the pairs and $4, 5$ the rungs; $N_{W}$ and $N_{R}$ are the pair and rung number operators; the sixteen is the even subspace, and its species reading, $
u^{c}, e^{c}, Q, L, u^{c}, d^{c}$ at (rungs, pairs) $= (0,0), (2,0), (1,1), (1,3), (0,2), (2,2)$, is the Standard-Model paper's under Hypothesis (S) \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT12}, so that every statement below naming a species carries (S); $B$ is the $\so(10)$-invariant bilinear pairing \cite[Lem.~9.23]{ButlerT12}; and for an odd element $T$ of the Clifford algebra of the ten, the \emph{mass form} is $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ on the sixteen. The operator $B - L := 1 - 	frac23 N_{W}$ takes the values $(1, 1, 	frac13, -1, -	frac13, -	frac13)$ on $(
u^{c}, e^{c}, Q, L, u^{c}, d^{c})$: $B - L$ is an affine function of the pair number (script). The decomposition of $16 \otimes 16$ and the dictionary between grades and $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ representations are stated as Fact \claimref{families.imported-decomposition-grade-dictionary} at the end of the section.

title: The $126$ doublet direction in the module, and the Georgi-Jarlskog Clebsch
proof: (i): $N_{W} = \sum_{i\le3} v_{i}w_{i} = \sum_{i\le3}(v_{i}\wedge w_{i} + \tfrac12)$ since $v_{i}\cdot w_{i} = \tfrac12$, so $1 - \tfrac23 N_{W} = -\tfrac23\sum v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$. For the rung: $w_{4}(1 - 2v_{4}w_{4}) = w_{4} - 2(1 - v_{4}w_{4})w_{4} = -w_{4}$ using $w_{4}^{2} = 0$, so $w_{4}\chi = -w_{4}(1 - 2n_{4})(1 - 2n_{5}) = w_{4}(1 - 2n_{5}) = -2w_{4}(v_{5}\wedge w_{5})$. The three factors $w_{4}$, $v_{5}\wedge w_{5}$, $\sum v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$ are built from mutually orthogonal vectors ($w_{4}$ anticommutes with $v_{5}, w_{5}$ and with every pair vector; the rung plane is orthogonal to the pair space), so their Clifford product is their wedge and has grade $1 + 2 + 2 = 5$. The script verifies the operator identity $T_{\mathrm{GJ}} = \tfrac43 w_{4}(v_{5}\wedge w_{5})(\sum v_{i}\wedge w_{i})$ on the module, the anticommutations, and, independently, the grade decomposition of $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ by the trace formula in the orthonormal basis $a_{i} = v_{i} + w_{i}$, $b_{i} = v_{i} - w_{i}$ of $\Cl(5,5)$ (coefficient of the blade $\Gamma_{A}$ is $\mathrm{tr}(\Gamma_{A}^{-1}T)/32$, the blades being trace-orthogonal in the irreducible representation), finding grade five only. The last clause of (i) is Fact \claimref{families.imported-decomposition-grade-dictionary} applied to the map $T \mapsto Y_{T}$, which is $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$-equivariant because $B$ is invariant: the grade-five space is $126 \oplus \overline{126}$, the bilinear forms on the sixteen are $16 \otimes 16 = 10 \oplus 120 \oplus 126$, and the $\overline{126}$ component, having no isomorphic summand among them, is sent to zero by Schur's lemma. (ii): with the species names that Hypothesis (S) supplies (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), $Y_{T_{\mathrm{GJ}}}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, w_{4}\varphi)\cdot(B - L)(\varphi)\chi(\varphi)$ since $B - L$ and $\chi$ are diagonal; on $(L, e^{c})$ the factor is $(B-L)(e^{c})\chi(e^{c}) = 1\cdot(-1)$ in one order and $(B-L)(L)\chi(L) = (-1)(+1)$ in the other, on $(Q, d^{c})$ it is $(-\tfrac13)(-1)$ and $(\tfrac13)(+1)$: equal in both orders, which is the symmetry, with the stated values times the $\pm1$ of $Y_{w_{4}}$. The script enumerates the form and checks symmetry and hypercharge conservation entry by entry. (iii): without $\chi$ the two orders carry $(B-L)(e^{c}) = 1$ and $(B-L)(L) = -1$, opposite signs; the script checks antisymmetry and the neutrality sums. (iv) is the same computation with $v_{4}$; the script enumerates the form, checks its symmetry, and records the signed entries, $+1$ on both $(L, \nu^{c})$ entries and $-\tfrac13$, $+\tfrac13$ on the $(Q, u^{c})$ entries according to colour, which is why only the magnitude is stated.

title: Imported: the tree relations, the family no-go, and the two other no-gos
The order of operations in the matter programme
text: Under Hypothesis (S), which supplies the species names, the family breaking cannot come first: by Fact \claimref{families.imported-tree-relations-family-no-go}(i) the family breaking acting on a $10$-vev leaves $m_{\mu} = m_{s}$ and $m_{e} = m_{d}$ exactly, and the observed second family needs the factor $3$ at the unification scale (Fact \claimref{families.imported-tree-relations-family-no-go}). Among one-family mass forms the factor is available in the module as the direction of Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}, and only there: the symmetric doublet mass forms of odd colour-singlet elements with the doublet's charges span the two-dimensional space of the $10$ form and the $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ form \cite[Prop.~9.32]{ButlerT12}. With three families there is a second source, the one-sided weighting of Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}(iii), whose antisymmetric form gives no one-family mass but does give entries between families through an antisymmetric family coupling (Fact \claimref{families.imported-grade-three-direction-between-families}). That direction requires the electroweak vev to couple not as a bare rung vector but as the rung vector wedged with the other rung's area bivector and with the pair-sector $\uu(1)$ generator. So the first result required of the weight programme is not a family texture but a \emph{pair-number-dependent rung coupling}: a derivation, from the mass mechanism, of a term of the form $w_{4}\wedge(v_{5}\wedge w_{5})\wedge\sum v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$ alongside the bare $w_{4}$, with the ratio of the two coefficients then fixing $m_{\mu}/m_{s}$ and $m_{e}/m_{d}$ jointly (the third family is where the bare $10$ relation $m_{b} \approx m_{\tau}$ is approximately right). Both sources carry the pair-number current, so the requirement stands on the route the Standard-Model paper registers, where the second family's factor comes through mixing with the third by the grade-three source and the role of that ratio passes to the coupling between the two families (Fact \claimref{families.imported-grade-three-direction-between-families}). The family breaking is the second step, acting on the resulting two-term structure; this is the order the capstone's table of open directions records for the matter programme \cite[Table~4]{ButlerT17}.
proof: Immediate from Fact \claimref{families.imported-tree-relations-family-no-go}(i), read with the species names that Hypothesis (S) supplies (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}, the uniqueness statement of \cite[Prop.~9.32]{ButlerT12} (\claimref{standard-model.space-symmetric-doublet-mass-forms-two}) and the imported factor, with Fact \claimref{families.imported-grade-three-direction-between-families} for the three-family sentences; the last clause is the standard reading of the Georgi-Jarlskog relation and is recorded at that level. The family breaking of the section ``The Koide geometry'' and the section ``The Gaussian theorems'' is unaffected by this: it acts on whichever two-term structure the mass mechanism supplies, and the modulus $\delta$ of successor problem (3) is read off the result.

title: What the series holds, and what the bracket cannot do
text: Each factor of the $126$ direction exists in the series: the rung vector is the Standard-Model paper's transported frozen point \cite[Prop.~9.27]{ButlerT12}, the slot area bivector $v_{5}\wedge w_{5}$ is the object whose expectation the grip computes, the symplectic area of the slot doublet \cite[Thm.~9.11]{ButlerT12}, and $\sum v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$ is the pair-number generator, the $B - L$ current. The product is not derived in the series as a coupling, and Fact \claimref{families.imported-tree-relations-family-no-go}(ii), (iii) say that neither the frozen point with its lifts nor the mass bracket with its composites produces it: the bracket direction couples through the $120$ or the $126$ \cite[Prop.~9.15(b)]{ButlerT12}, but along the $e^{c}$ direction, of hypercharge $+1$ (the script reads $Y(e^{c}) = 1$), and a mass form $B(\psi, T\varphi)$ conserving hypercharge needs $Y(T) = -(Y(\psi) + Y(\varphi)) = \pm\tfrac12$ on the Yukawa pairs, so a direction of charge one is not a neutral vev, and its neutral composites with the rung vectors are rung-sector objects insensitive to $B - L$. The weight spectrum therefore cannot be addressed until the dynamics of the rung coupling is known, as the levels of the results say, but the obstruction now has a definite form: one grade-five term, three factors, all present, and the missing coupling is specifically that of the rung vector to the pair-sector $\uu(1)$ current, which is what the Standard-Model paper's colour label carries and what Hypothesis (S) would have to produce. The face-family conjecture of the section ``Three faces'' and the condensation of the section ``Condensation and the ordering'' supply the family matrix $F$; they cannot supply the factor, and this section says why.

title: Imported: the decomposition of $16 \otimes 16$ and the grade dictionary
text: For the positive-chirality spinor $16$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, $16 \otimes 16 = 10 \oplus 120 \oplus 126$, the $10$ and the $126$ symmetric and the $120$ antisymmetric. In the Clifford algebra of the ten the odd grades carry the representations $1 \leftrightarrow 10$, $3 \leftrightarrow 120$ and $5 \leftrightarrow 126 \oplus \overline{126}$, the grade-five space splitting into its self-dual and anti-self-dual halves; of these only the self-dual half, the $126$, pairs the positive-chirality $16$ with itself, and the $\overline{126}$ acts as zero in any $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$-equivariant bilinear form on the $16$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Slansky1981}; standard representation theory, not proved in the series. The script checks purity of grade five and the symmetry and entries of the induced form, not the decomposition.

title: Imported: the grade-three direction between families, and the registered route
text: The one-sided weightings $w_{4}(B - L)$ and $v_{4}(B - L)$ are pure grade three, so their forms lie in the $120$ component of $16 \otimes 16$ (Fact \claimref{families.imported-decomposition-grade-dictionary}); they couple exactly $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, respectively $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, with lepton-to-quark modulus ratio $3$; and with a family matrix antisymmetric in the family indices, as a $120$ couples, the combined form is symmetric and vanishes on the family diagonal, so the direction contributes only to entries between different families. title: Successor problems
text: Six, the first the registered open problem. (1) \emph{The non-Gaussian completion:} produce the $207$ from caused structure, under the relabelling-signature refutation condition; this is the family programme's terminal open item and the paper's declared open problem, and by Corollary \claimref{families.order-operations-matter-programme} it is the second step, acting on whatever two-term structure the mass mechanism supplies. (2) \emph{The Gram-square structure:} derive that the full three-family Yukawa form is the square of a face-space map, promoted from convenience to necessity by the order-one angle; Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(3) and the whole of the section ``The Gaussian theorems'' assume it. (3) \emph{The second-order breaking's modulus:} the free phase $\delta = 0.222$ encodes $m_{\mu}/m_{e}$ and is the genuine $S_{2} \to 1$ stage; its computation depends on (1) and, by Corollary \claimref{families.order-operations-matter-programme}, on the coefficient of the $126$ direction relative to the $10$, which the breaking acts on and cannot supply. (5) \emph{The dressing:} compute the strong dressing that spoils the quark relation, converting the selectivity account into a derivation. (6) \emph{The absolute scale, in three pieces, and the pair-sector current:} Proposition \claimref{families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail} dissolves the absolute scale into $N$, the rung unit and the Yukawa pattern, the first two assigned to the Standard-Model paper's successors (5) and (1) and kinematically not functions of each other. title: Mass as symplectic area: the two-spinor formula
The mass-weight dictionary
text:
Let $\sigma$ be a density of conformal weight $w$ on a vacuum Einstein background with frozen point $I$, and impose the coupling
\[
I \cdot D\sigma = 0.
\]
Then, in the scale of $I$, $\sigma$ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation $(\Box + m^{2})\sigma = 0$ with
\begin{equation}
m^{2} = -\,w(w+n-1)\,Q(I), \qquad\text{in } n = 4:\quad m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = -\,w(w+3)\,H^{2}.
\end{equation}
The mass of a field is its conformal weight, read in the units the frozen point provides, and every mass in the theory is $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ times a factor fixed by the weight.

title: The bracket composite lands on the $10$
text:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the unital algebra generated, inside the endomorphisms of the five-mode module, by the frozen point $I = av_{1} + bw_{1}$, its lifted rung components $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$, the bracket $b = v_{4}v_{5}$ and its conjugate $b^{\dagger} = w_{5}w_{4}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\dim \mathcal{A} = 32$, and $\mathcal{A} = \Cl_{R} \oplus I\,\Cl_{R}$ where $\Cl_{R} \cong \Cl(2,2)_{\C}$ is the sixteen-dimensional algebra of the two rung modes.
\item[(ii)] The colour-singlet part of $\mathcal{A}$, the commutant of $\su(3)$ acting on the pair modes, is exactly $\Cl_{R}$.
\item[(iii)] The odd elements of $\Cl_{R}$ of hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$ form the two-dimensional space spanned by $w_{4}$ and $w_{4}N_{5}$.
\item[(iv)] The mass form of $w_{4}N_{5}$ is one half the mass form of $w_{4}$. Hence every symmetric doublet mass form produced by $\mathcal{A}$ is a multiple of the $10$ form, with $|y_{e}| = |y_{d}|$ under Hypothesis (S), which names the species; in particular the neutral composite $b^{\dagger}v_{5} = -w_{4} + w_{4}N_{5}$ has mass form $-\tfrac12$ times the $10$ form.
\item[(v)] The $126$ direction $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ is not in the span of the forms $\mathcal{A}$ produces, and the pair bivector $\sum_{i} v_{i} \wedge w_{i}$ is not in $\mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Chirality: the two halves of the spinor module, and conjugation as duality
text: The conformal spinor space $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ (twistor space) and its partner $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves of the ascended Dirac module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the sector of a single conformal spinor $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is their direct sum. Under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ the two halves carry different content: $\CS$ carries $(1)_{0} \oplus (\bar{3})_{-2/3}$ and $\CSm{}$ carries $(3)_{-1/3} \oplus (1)_{-1}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3)), so the two halves are inequivalent representations of the group: the chirality split is visible to the internal symmetry, not only to the grading. The singlet spectrum listed by a single handedness is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(2)'s, and in particular the colour content $3 \oplus \bar{3}$ of the two halves becomes $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$ under it, which is the conjugation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}. Moreover the conjugation is an operation inside the pair system: the dual of the grade-$k$ state is the grade-$(3-k)$ state with the full-system phase removed, $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes (\Lambda^{3}W)^{*}$, of weight $+2k$; and the two doublets at the level of one conformal spinor of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) are each other's duals, $(\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W)^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}W$, and under (S) have opposite parity. Under (S) they are therefore one doublet and its antiparticle, not two candidates, and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(1)'s listing choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}.

title: A grade-three Georgi-Jarlskog direction
text: Under Hypothesis (S), $w_{4}(B - L)$ and $v_{4}(B - L)$ are pure grade three, so their forms lie in the $120$ component of $16 \otimes 16$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears}, with the equivariance of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}). Their mass forms on the sixteen are antisymmetric and couple exactly $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, respectively $(L, \nu^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$, with lepton-to-quark modulus ratio $3$. With an antisymmetric family matrix the combined form is symmetric and vanishes on the family diagonal: the direction contributes only to entries between different families.

title: Hypothesis (S): slot statistics, derived from the slot-module hypothesis
text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

title: Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). The $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ anomaly coefficient of the two doublets, $3Y_{Q} + Y_{L}$ with the three the colour multiplicity, is then the identity $3 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac12 = 0$; it would equal $1$ if the empty conformal spinor were listed as the particle instead, so the anomaly confirms the orientation the listing fixed. Pair counting fixes $|Y_{L}/Y_{Q}| = 3$; the parity fixes the sign.
\item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives
\[
(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},
\]
that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. (The listing by the opposite handedness is the conjugate of this one, the same spectrum in the opposite convention.) Under (S) the grade-$k$ states of a single conformal spinor are the $(0, k)$ components, the states with no slot mode and $k$ pair modes occupied (their content $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and weight $-2k$ match, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight), so their parity is the total parity and this listing is the same listing as in (1).
\item (Consistency, and uniqueness given the content; under (S) for the doublets.) With the content of (1) and (2), all four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} hold. Conversely, for the field content $Q = (2,3)$, $L = (2,1)$, $u^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $d^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $e^{c} = (1,1)$, all listed in one handedness, together with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or no fourth singlet, and $Y_{Q} = 1/6$ as the normalisation, the four conditions determine $Y_{L}$, $Y(e^{c})$ and $\{Y(u^{c}), Y(d^{c})\}$ uniquely, and the solution is the spectrum of (1) and (2). Both hypotheses are necessary: with a fourth singlet of unconstrained hypercharge the conditions admit a one-parameter family, and if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$ rather than zero.
\end{enumerate}

title: The internal symmetry ladder
text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form''.)

title: The mass bracket is a charged singlet
text:
Under the $U(2)$ of the two-spinor step (two conformal spinors, mixed by their slot index), the mass bracket transforms by the determinant:
\[
\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} \mapsto \det(U) \cdot \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}.
\]
It is therefore an $SU(2)$ singlet carrying charge one under the determinant character (charge two under the scalar phase $e^{I_{6}\theta}\,\id$, whose determinant is $e^{2I_{6}\theta}$, with $I_{6}$ the complex unit of $\CS$): its modulus is the mass (Fact \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}), its phase is pure gauge under the $U(1)$, and it vanishes exactly on the massless locus. Under the global form of the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form'', with the hypercharge of the section ``Content, charges, chirality'', the bracket of two conformal spinors, each the vacuum of its pair system, transforms as $(1, 1)$ with abelian weight $6$, hypercharge $Y = +1$: the quantum numbers of $e^{c}$, and not those of a weak doublet. (The bracket is defined on conformal spinors; what it would be for an excited composite depends on the state space, and is not defined here.)

title: No-go: the frozen point and its lifts do not generate the $126$ direction
text: Let $I$ be the frozen point, a vector of the first rung's hyperbolic plane inside the pair space $W \oplus \overline{W}$ (in mode terms $I = a\,v_{1} + b\,w_{1}$ with $Q(I) = ab$), and let $c_{4} = -w_{4} + \lambda v_{4}$ and $c_{5} = -w_{5}$ be the rung components of its two lifts (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}, $\lambda = \Lambda/3$). Then the unital associative algebra generated by $\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}\}$ is eight-dimensional, spanned by $1, I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}, Ic_{5}, c_{4}c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}$, its odd part is $\mathrm{span}\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}\}$, and of these $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$ are grade one (the $10$) while $I$ and $Ic_{4}c_{5}$ carry a pair-mode index and are not colour singlets. The algebra contains no colour-singlet doublet direction beyond the $10$, hence not $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$; and the pair-sector $u(1)$ bivector $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$, the factor $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ needs, is not in it.

title: One vev vector: the $10_{H}$ relations with up-type masses read through the conjugate, the breaking pattern, and the split
text:
Under Hypothesis (S), let $c = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$ be a fixed vector of the rung plane and $M_{c}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, c\varphi)$ the resulting mass form on the sixteen. Then the nonzero entries of $M_{c}$ have magnitude $|a|$ on $(L, 
u^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$ and $|b|$ on $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$. The up-type masses, and with them the neutrino's Dirac mass, are read through the conjugate $c^{*} =  ar{b}\,v_{4} +  ar{a}\,w_{4}$ of the tower's conjugation ($v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$, Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}), as the Standard Model gives up-type masses through the conjugate doublet: they are the entries of $M_{c^{*}}$ on $(Q, u^{c})$ and $(L, 
u^{c})$, the coupling to $c^{*}$, of magnitude $|a(c^{*})| = |b|$ with $a(c^{*})$ the $v_{4}$ coefficient of $c^{*}$, while the down-type and charged-lepton masses are the entries of $M_{c}$. So at tree level $m_{
u} = m_{u} = |b|$ and $m_{e} = m_{d} = |b|$: one coupling gives all four Dirac masses equal, the relations of a single real $10$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears}), and the neutrino's Dirac mass is the up-type mass, as the neutrino paper's top-like valuation takes it (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-ceiling-under-hypothesis-u-arrow}). Read through $c$ itself the up-type entry would be $|a|$, with $m_{u}/m_{d} = |a|/|b|$ set by the direction of $c$; on the null-lift locus that reading gives the product law $m_{u}m_{d} = \Lambda/3$, which the observed top and bottom masses rule out (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), and it is not the series' reading. Under the reading through $c^{*}$ the direction of $c$ no longer separates up-type from down-type masses: the observed up-down hierarchy needs a second coupling or another source. The $v_{4}$ term couples only the $T_{3} = -	frac12$ components of $L$ and $Q$ and the $w_{4}$ term only the $T_{3} = +	frac12$ components: a vector along one rung breaks the slot $SU(2) 	imes U(1)_{Y}$ to the $U(1)$ that fixes it, the electroweak pattern. And doublet-triplet splitting, the requirement that the triplet partner of the doublet not acquire a vev and not stay light, is the requirement that the vector lie in the rung directions and not in the ground ones: the split is between what transport adjoined and what the ground completion already had.

title: Quarks and leptons: the two-level fermion content
The space of symmetric doublet mass forms is two-dimensional
text: Under Hypothesis (S), on the sixteen of one generation, the symmetric bilinear forms $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ with $T$ an odd colour-singlet element of the Clifford algebra of the ten carrying hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$ span exactly a two-dimensional space, spanned by the form of the $10$ direction $w_{4}$ (Clebsch ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 1$) and the form of $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (ratio $3$). Every form in the space couples only $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, and the ratio $y_{e}/y_{d}$ takes every value as the two coefficients vary: the representation theory fixes the two directions and not the ratio.

title: The trichotomy: what kind of number $N$ is
text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
At observation level, two competing effects are then named without being balanced: an entropic weighting of the freezing by $\exp(S_{\Lambda}) = \exp(\pi N^{2})$, with $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ the cosmological horizon's area-law entropy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), favours large $N$ overwhelmingly (the well-known entropic argument for small $\Lambda$, inherited with every one of its known objections, listed as inherited and not solved), while at the endpoint $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null and the curvature-squared presentation of the action, whose prefactor is $3/\Lambda$, does not exist; the action paper is explicit that this is a boundary of the presentation and not of the action, the Einstein-Cartan functional remaining \cite[Thm.~3.1, Rem.~3.2]{ButlerT10}, so what is lost at $\Lambda = 0$ is the reductive structure and the frozen point's length, not gravity. Large because large boundary mode spaces dominate the measure; nonzero because the descent selects a frozen point of nonzero length; the value is the balance point, and the balance point awaits the descent measure, the one object this framework does not possess. Last, a statement of units only, flagged as such: in the boundary modes' own units, qubits, one per rung of the Fock module (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), the horizon's capacity $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ qubits (the mode count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} under the black hole's counting rule), whose base-two logarithm is about $407$; the paper's $R = \log_{2} N^{2} \approx 405$ counts the rungs of a module of dimension $N^{2}$, whose capacity is only $\ln N^{2} = 2\ln N$ nats, not the horizon's. Neither number is a count of turns of the mod-8 clock, which no rung moves: each rung preserves the residue $p - q \pmod 8$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}). This is the question in the framework's own coordinates, not an answer to it.

title: The mass dictionary, coupling to the frozen point, explains the observed masses
text: Refuted. The corrected statement: It restates the hierarchy problem: every known massive particle has complex weight $-\tfrac32 \pm i\nu$ with $\nu \approx m/H$, and the question becomes why the imaginary parts of the conformal weights are so large in Hubble units.

title: The raw representation content matches the fermion table entry by entry
text: Refuted. The corrected statement: The disagreements are composites; generators, not states, are the content, and the lepton lies one level higher, under the declared hypothesis of slot statistics.

title: The vacuum omega-area sets the weak scale
text: Refuted. The corrected statement: It is wrong by between forty-four and one hundred and five orders of magnitude; the weak scale falls back to the weight question, and the vacuum alignment instead orders the families: democracy, rank one, one heavy.
